mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in workplace attendance observed in the last week indicates a broader return to out-of-home activities, which will directly translate to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility falls back to t-1w levels or lower in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in transit station activity, exceeding 10 percentage points, signals a critical mass of people resuming commutes and other out-of-home travel, directly boosting retail and recreation visits within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility remains above the 10-point threshold for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship between residential time and workplace attendance suggests people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This shift, when coupled with rising workplace mobility, will lead to increased discretionary spending and higher retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases while WORKPLACES mobility increases, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a period where policy restrictions are gradually easing, a sustained increase in parks visitation reflects growing public confidence in outdoor activities. This increased comfort will eventually extend to indoor public spaces, driving a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains above -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains relatively high due to policy easing but RETAIL_REC shows no improvement or further decline over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decline in residential mobility, following a period of sustained increase, indicates a shift away from staying at home. This sustained reduction in time spent at home will free up time for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses its recent decline and increases for two consecutive weeks, yet RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Stable or slightly increasing grocery and pharmacy visits, indicating essential needs are being met without significant disruption, provides a baseline of community activity that supports a gradual recovery in discretionary retail and recreation over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stays above -5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility drops below -5% for two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous strong rebound in both transit station activity and workplace attendance signifies a coordinated return to urban routines. This synergy will create a positive feedback loop, driving increased footfall and spending in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES mobility declines significantly in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent rebound in workplace and transit activity is short-lived, and residential mobility begins to rise again, it indicates a reversal of the trend towards out-of-home activities, leading to a decline in retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall by more than 5 points week-on-week, AND RESIDENTIAL rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise or stabilize, and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall or stabilize, but RETAIL_REC still declines over the next two weeks.
